prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State (Duty Manager declares); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase; Contingency Fallback State (Airport Duty Manager declares after consulting Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, System Support Engineer; entry: auth loss, time misalignment, corrupted data, surveillance/flight-data mismatch, advisory delivery failure; exit: stable service, consistent data, user access, affected leads agree). Fallback: Portal down→Digital Briefing Room, log decisions later. DPS/CAM unreliable→RFM uses last verified Airport Capacity Plan with Airspace Sector Planner, Meteorology Briefing Officer. SAE down→Slot Coordinator runs manual slots on control sheet at Contingency Operations Console; keeps last valid CTT unless safety/capacity/curfew/regulatory; revised CTT only after Tower Supervisor (runway) and Ramp Control Lead (surface) confirm; checks Crew Duty Extension Log; Airline Operations Coordinator, Aircraft Operator Representative acknowledge via voice readback/written. TSM, Ramp Movement Board advisory unless SSE confirms; DMS monitoring only, MUST NOT overwrite times; Arrival Regulation Console display only, RFM approves changes. SSE isolates failures, advises restoration; Data Governance Steward confirms trusted data, flags sync for reconciliation; ADM briefs via Digital Briefing Room. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (Emberline); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove); Identity Access Service; Collaborative Decision Log; Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf); Gate Conflict Detector; Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh ≤5 s); Common Situation Display; Audit Event Ledger; Business Rules Registry; Sector Load Monitor; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Weather Ingest Gateway

New part:
S736: Before returning automation to control, the Slot Coordinator reconciles the manual slot record with the Slot Allocation Engine and resolves any conflict in the Collaborative Decision Log.
S737: After restoration, the Performance Analytics Warehouse receives the outage timeline, manual intervention record, and recovery milestones for inclusion in the Post Operations Report.
S738: The system treats passenger disruption information as a secondary planning signal that can refine, but not replace, capacity and safety constraints in traffic flow decisions.
S739: Its purpose in this area is to help the Regional Flow Manager understand where a small metering adjustment may reduce downstream disruption without degrading the Airport Capacity Plan.
S740: Airline Operations Coordinator sends the Passenger Misconnect Count.
S741: The Airline Interface Adapter validates the timeliness, flight association, and airline ownership of connection-risk data before it is made available for operational use.
S742: The Data Governance Steward defines the acceptable aggregation level so that the Regional Flow Platform does not expose passenger names, booking references, or protected itinerary details.
S743: The Demand Prediction Service combines connection-risk indicators with aircraft readiness, scheduled bank structure, and forecast arrival variability to estimate the sensitivity of selected departures.
S744: These estimates are advisory and do not create an entitlement for a flight to receive a favorable Calculated Takeoff Time.
S745: The Slot Allocation Engine continues to apply the approved sequencing policy, runway capacity, airspace constraints, and published Ground Delay Program parameters as controlling inputs.
S746: When several flights have similar operational priority, connection-risk information may be used as a tie breaker if the Business Rules Registry permits that use for the active operating state.
S747: The Departure Metering Service can therefore recommend a minor hold, release, or resequencing action only when the change remains inside the available runway and surface movement envelope.
S748: The Tower Supervisor retains authority over tactical runway sequencing and may reject any advisory that would impair safe separation, wake spacing, or local controller workload.
S749: The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to determine whether a proposed metering adjustment can be supported by stand availability, pushback feasibility, and taxi route status.
S750: The Airport Duty Manager uses the Airport CDM Portal to see whether airline recovery actions are concentrated in one bank or distributed across the operating day.
S751: Typical airline recovery actions include flight retiming, aircraft substitution, passenger protection on later services, and selective holding of departures already inside normal operational tolerance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
